title: Accepted Artifact for Privacy-Respecting Type Error Telemetry at Scale
size_source: Zenodo record API files[] block, read 2026-09-20
rows_stated: over 1.5 million telemetry records from over 340,000 sessions
rows_source: paper abstract at github.com/bennn/luau-telemetry/blob/master/programming23/abstract.txt, read 2026-09-20; NOT counted by me
authors: Greenman Ben; Jeffrey Alan (Roblox); Krishnamurthi Shriram (Brown University); Shah Mitesh (Roblox)
training_rows_yield: ZERO code rows. The abstract states the system deliberately cannot collect source code fragments, error messages or filepaths. A record is a timestamp, session id, send reason and a numeric summary of the most recent type analyses.
why_it_matters: Roblox's own published, CC-BY-licensed measurement of which Luau type errors real Studio creators actually hit and how often (paper Table 6, Type Error Popularity), plus type-error.rktd, a mapping from Luau type error codes to error names. This is the empirical weighting for a synthetic type-error-repair curriculum: it replaces a guess about what is hard with a measurement.
caveats: Spring 2023 collection window; the 2023 Luau type system is not the 2026 one. Aggregate counts are in the repo out/ directory but the repo itself carries no SPDX licence (GitHub API license: null) while the Zenodo record is cc-by-4.0 - cite the Zenodo record, not the repo.
verified_by: Zenodo REST API record fetch; GitHub tree listing of bennn/luau-telemetry@master; read abstract.txt and artifact/README.md

reason: Description field is EMPTY (hasDescription true, description ''), zero tags, usability 0.25. It is one of a 'Slim Stack <language>' family by the same uploader (slim-stack-coffeescript also observed), i.e. a per-language re-upload of BigCode's The Stack. The Stack is licence:other with per-file original licences and a creator opt-out mechanism; restamping that as CC0 discards both the per-file notices and the opt-out. This is the exact compilation-licence-vs-file-licence trap. A CC0 tag someone typed into a form is not a licence grant over 983 MB of other people's code.

files_measured: 2218 .lua/.luau files across the 19 MIT repos listed individually above
measure_source: summed by me from per-repo recursive tree listings read 2026-09-20
reason: ROLLUP ROW - do not count alongside its members. The headline: Roblox's own org publishes a currently-maintained, MIT-licensed, first-party Luau codebase of roughly 15009245 bytes across 2218 files, most of it pushed within the last month. v1 sourced 24,411 code records from two aggregated Hugging Face corpora of contested provenance. This body has an unambiguous licence from the entity that defines the language, and none of it appears in the 60 Hugging Face dispositions or, by its nature, in the 159 community GitHub leads.
honest_limit: These are libraries and framework ports. They teach idiomatic modern Luau, typing, testing and module architecture. They do NOT teach gameplay, Studio workflows, monetisation, DataStores under contention, or anything a player sees. They are a quality floor, not a frontier corpus.
overlap_risk: The GitHub-leads sweeper may reach some of these. Deduplicate against that register before acquisition.
verified_by: 19 individual gh tree listings

measure_source: gh recursive tree of master, summed by me 2026-09-20
reason: 'All of ROBLOX's core client scripts' under Apache-2.0. This is the engine's own client-side UI, input, chat and player code written by Roblox engineers - 3.0 MB of it.
caveat: LAST PUSHED 2020-06-10. Six years stale. It predates the task library becoming idiomatic, modern UI primitives, and most of the 2021-2026 API surface. As a source of ARCHITECTURE and first-party idiom it is strong; as a source of CURRENT API usage it will actively teach deprecated calls. Admit only with per-symbol currency checks against the 2026 API dump, and consider it a pretraining-only source. The same currency objection Apple already sustained against Roblox/luau_corpus (2023) applies here with three more years of drift.

measure_source: gh recursive tree of master, summed by me 2026-09-20; tree not truncated
reason: This is the single best answer to the owner's 'every modern Luau construct' ask that I found. 92 RFCs, ~498 KB, each documenting one language feature with its motivation, design, alternatives considered and drawbacks. That is the provenance for string interpolation, generalised iteration, compound assignment, type functions, and every other construct that separates Luau from Lua - written by the people who added them. No aggregated corpus contains the REASONING behind a construct; this does.
blocker: No licence file. Public visibility is not a reuse grant. This needs either a licence clarification from luau-lang or a decision to treat RFCs as retrieval-only reference (which is what Apple's existing policy already does for Roblox/creator-docs).
suggested_disposition: Retrieval-reference track, matching the existing creator-docs treatment, unless a licence is obtained.

rows_stated: 'over 1.5 million trajectories'; card text states 'synthesized from 495 real-world Model Context Protocols (MCPs) spanning 2,000+ tools'; size_categories tag 1M<n<10M
rows_source: dataset card via hub_repo_details, read 2026-09-20; NOT counted by me
reason: The product's hardest capability is not writing Luau, it is behaving correctly as a Studio agent: planning, calling a tool, reading the observation, recovering from a failed call, cancelling. v1 has 153 tool-trajectory rows total (123/17/13 train/val/test, measured by me today). Apache-2.0 and fully synthetic means no rights entanglement, and the trajectories involve real tool executions rather than authored outcomes - which is precisely the property the v1 register flags as missing from Pinkstack/RobloxAgent-toolreason.
admission_conditions: Shape transfer ONLY, and this must be stated in the dataset card: the tools are MCP tools, not Studio tools. Mixing these rows in unlabelled will teach the model to hallucinate tool names that do not exist in the plugin's schema. The defensible use is either (a) a small, deliberately-weighted mix to teach the multi-step call/observe/recover LOOP while Roblox-specific rows teach the schema, or (b) a template source whose tool schemas are rewritten to the plugin's real schema - in which case the executions are no longer real and the rows must be relabelled synthetic-unverified.
caveats: 'Real tool executions' is the card's claim. I did not replay any trajectory. Per the project's own rule, a README claim is a claim until replay proves it.
verified_by: hub_repo_details overview read

rows_stated: '60,000 data collected by APIGen'; card states verification 'through three hierarchical stages: format checking, actual function executions, and semantic verification' and 'human evaluation over 600 sampled data points'
rows_source: dataset card via hub_repo_details, read 2026-09-20; NOT counted by me
reason: The most carefully verified function-calling set I found, and the verification design is the point: format check, then ACTUAL EXECUTION, then semantic check. That three-stage gate is a directly transferable blueprint for how the Roblox tool-trajectory track should be validated - which the coverage contract lists under tool-trajectories as 'real observations, failed tool calls, recovery, cancellation, unsupported operations' with zero accepted examples so far.
admission_conditions: Same schema-mismatch warning as Toucan. Single-turn call generation, not multi-step agent loops - complements Toucan rather than duplicating it. 600 of 60,000 human-evaluated means 1% human coverage; the other 99% rests on the automated gates.
verified_by: hub_repo_details overview read

blocker: Since 2024-07-12 the official dump is no longer posted publicly to archive.org. It is behind a login, and the downloader must AGREE that 'the file is being provided to me for my own use and for projects that do not include training a large language model'. That is an express anti-LLM-training condition on the distribution channel.
the_actual_question: CC BY-SA 4.0 is an irrevocable licence on the CONTENT; the download gate is a contractual condition on one CHANNEL. Whether a pre-2024 archive.org mirror escapes a term you would be agreeing to today is a real legal question and it is not mine to answer. Do not treat the old mirror as a clean bypass, and do not click through the agreement and then train on it.
volume_reality_check: Even if cleared, the Roblox-specific yield is small: ~2,300 roblox + 188 luau + 123 roblox-studio questions. Low thousands, not tens of thousands. Roblox developers ask on the DevForum, not Stack Overflow. The 22,931 lua questions are mostly not Luau. Attribution under BY-SA at row granularity is also a real engineering burden.
recommendation: Route to counsel with the exact agreement text. Do not acquire in the meantime. Given the volume reality check, this is not worth much legal spend.

reason: This is the highest-volume Roblox source in existence and the least defensible. 'Uncopylocked' means a creator left copy-protection off, which grants copying INSIDE Studio. It is not a redistribution or training licence, it is frequently an oversight, and it is revocable in practice by flipping the setting - which a downloaded archive does not honour. Worse, the wiki states plainly that older versions can be pulled via the Asset Delivery API regardless, and that 'Older games most likely have their protection off' - i.e. the archive's contents are not filtered by creator intent at all.
why_recorded: Recorded precisely because it is the obvious thing a volume-hungry sweep would grab: real places, real scripts, real gameplay, enormous scale. A register of rejections is worth as much as a register of acquisitions, and this is the one most likely to be re-proposed.

measure_source: python json load of verified-modules.json, counted by me 2026-09-20
card_note_verbatim: Luau modules this repository authored. Every one was RUN against its own exhaustive checks at build time; a module that failed is absent rather than shipped unverified.
record_shape: each module carries id, family, and a precise natural-language contract (e.g. purchase-transaction / economy-transaction, with a full pre/post-condition contract)
yield_reasoning: 80 modules x roughly 8-15 defensible row shapes each: implement-from-contract, repair-a-mutant, explain-the-contract, write-the-test, identify-the-violated-precondition. The ceiling is set by 80 DISTINCT BEHAVIOURS. Past roughly 15 variants per module you are producing renamed-variable clones, which the coverage contract explicitly names as forbidden count inflation.
what_makes_a_row_trustworthy: The mutant must be generated mechanically (not by a model) and CONFIRMED to fail the module's existing exhaustive check, and the repaired version confirmed to pass. That is a two-sided machine verdict with no model in the loop. Every row carries the check's exit status as a receipt.
what_would_make_it_untrustworthy: A model writing both the bug and the fix and a model judging the result. Then the row asserts nothing.
verified_by: direct file read and count, 2026-09-20

measured: 29 files carrying a references array; 384 reference rows; 2,447 demonstrates claims; 813 rules; 54 gapsAgainstShippedTheme
measure_source: python walk of ui-references/*.json, summed by me 2026-09-20
DISCREPANCY_WITH_BRIEF: The task brief states 2,353 claims across 28 files. I measured 2,447 across 29 files today and could not reproduce 2,353 by excluding any single file (closest single-file exclusions land at 2,343 or 2,350). The brief's figure is likely from an earlier snapshot. I am reporting what I measured, not the brief's number.
provenance_quality: Strong. Each reference row names a URL that was actually fetched and the date, and the files' own provenance note states that no image, Luau source, asset id or sentence of anyone's UI is stored - only the construction convention read out of what each page describes.
yield_reasoning: 2,447 claims is not 2,447 rows. Claims cluster hard - screen-social alone holds 162, many restating the same convention. Honest deduplication to DISTINCT, mechanically-checkable construction decisions leaves an estimated 600-1,000 constraints; at 2-3 row shapes each that is 1,500-3,000. The estimate is mine and the deduplication has not been done.
what_makes_a_row_trustworthy: Three things together: (1) compiles under --!strict; (2) satisfies a STATIC property check derived from the claim, e.g. uses UIListLayout rather than absolute offsets, or calls GuiService:GetGuiInset() before positioning against the top edge; (3) carries the citation URL of the claim it implements.
the_hard_limit: NONE OF THESE ARE VISUALLY VERIFIED. This project's own standing rule is that technically-correct-but-ugly output gets rejected, and that the pixels are the evidence. A UI that compiles and satisfies a layout predicate can still be ugly. These rows teach CONVENTION, not taste, and the dataset card must say so rather than letting a reader infer visual quality from a passing gate.
verified_by: direct file walk and count, 2026-09-20

yield_reasoning: Bounded by (distinct Luau type error codes) x (distinct code contexts in which each plausibly arises). Neither factor is read - the error-code table is type-error.rktd in the artifact and I did not unpack it - so this range is an estimate and marked as one.
the_idea: Synthesise broken/fixed Luau pairs, but choose WHICH errors to synthesise using Roblox's own published measurement of what real Studio creators actually hit (paper Table 6, Type Error Popularity) rather than a guess about what is hard. The artifact also ships type-error.rktd, a mapping from Luau type error codes to error names.
what_makes_a_row_trustworthy: A two-sided compiler verdict with no model in the loop: the BROKEN version must fail luau-analyze with the SPECIFIC expected error code, and the FIXED version must pass. If either side does not do what it is supposed to, the row is discarded rather than kept with a caveat. This is the only synthesis lane here where the verifier is fully mechanical on both sides.
dependency: Pin the exact Luau toolchain version. An error code's meaning is a property of a compiler release, and luau-lang/luau moves. A row verified against an unpinned 'latest' asserts nothing six months later.
currency_caveat: The telemetry was collected Spring 2023. Error frequencies from the 2023 type system are a prior about the 2026 one, not a measurement of it. Use it to rank, not to claim coverage.

measure_source: wc -l and ls -la, run by me 2026-09-20
honest_yield: ZERO additional trustworthy rows from synthesis alone.
why: This is the lane where this project already has a documented defect on record: never fill missing tool results with invented success messages. A trajectory's value is entirely in the OBSERVATION - what the tool actually returned, including when it failed. A synthesised observation is a fabricated measurement, which is the single worst defect available here. Generating 10,000 trajectories whose tool outputs a model made up would be worse than having 153.
the_unlock: Roblox/open-cloud-execution-binary-payloads-example (MIT) and Roblox/place-ci-cd-demo (MIT), both recorded in this register, demonstrate the Open Cloud Luau Execution API. That API can produce REAL execution receipts. Trajectories captured through it are measurements, not synthesis, and the coverage contract's tool-trajectories aspects (real observations, failed tool calls, recovery, cancellation, unsupported operations) become reachable. That is a capability the build needs to acquire, not a corpus it can find.
